nanananda_verbatim:
It is as if one is trying to outstrip one's shadow by running towards
it out of fun, while the other is trying to flee from it out of fear.
plain_english_below: It is as if one is trying to outstrip one's shadow by running towards it out of fun, while the other is trying to flee from it out of fear.
tts_line: It is as if one is trying to outstrip one's shadow by running towards it out of fun, while the other is trying to flee from it out of fear.

nanananda_verbatim:
Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting
of the three is contact. Because of contact, feeling. What one feels,
one perceives. What one perceives, one reasons about. What one reasons
about, one turns into papañca. What one turns into papañca, owing to
that papañcasaññāsankhā beset him.

The comparison of this discourse to a honey-ball is understandable,
since it holds the secret of the latent tendencies towards dogmatic
views.
Just as if a man overcome by hunger came upon a honey-ball.

When vitakka breaks loose and runs riot, it creates a certain deluded
  state of mind, which is papanca.
plain_english_below: Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is where senses hit the world. Because of where senses hit the world, pleasant-or-unpleasant tone. What one feels, one perceives. What one perceives, one reasons about. What one reasons about, one turns into papanca. What one turns into papanca, owing to that papancasannasankha beset him. / The comparison of this discourse to a honey-ball is understandable, since it holds the secret of the latent tendencies towards dogmatic views. / Just as if a man overcome by hunger came upon a honey-ball. / When vitakka breaks loose and runs riot, it creates a certain deluded state of mind, which is papanca.
tts_line: Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. The meeting of the three is where senses hit the world. Because of where senses hit the world, pleasant-or-unpleasant tone. What one feels, one perceives. What one perceives, one reasons about. What one reasons about, one turns into papanca. What one turns into papanca, owing to that papancasannasankha beset him.. The comparison of this discourse to a honey-ball is understandable, since it holds the secret of the latent tendencies towards dogmatic views.. Just as if a man overcome by hunger came upon a honey-ball.. When vitakka breaks loose and runs riot, it creates a certain deluded state of mind, which is papanca.

nanananda_verbatim:
The worldlings under the sway of defilements, which thrive on the
perception of the compact, ghanasaññā, have the habit of grasping
everything... he regards the world as a unit due to his perception of
the compact, as he takes cognizance only of the arising aspect,
ignoring the decaying aspect.
plain_english_below: The worldlings under the sway of defilements, which thrive on the perception of the compact, ghanasanna, have the habit of holding on everything... he regards the world as a unit due to his perception of the compact, as he takes cognizance only of the arising aspect, ignoring the decaying aspect.
tts_line: The worldlings under the sway of defilements, which thrive on the perception of the compact, ghanasanna, have the habit of holding on everything... he regards the world as a unit due to his perception of the compact, as he takes cognizance only of the arising aspect, ignoring the decaying aspect.

nanananda_verbatim:
There is a malignantly pervert idea, ingrained in saṃsāric beings,
known as the perception of permanence in the impermanent, anicce
niccasaññā, which prevents them from seeing the inherent transience of
eye and forms. That is how the six spheres of sense create a world
before us.
plain_english_below: There is a malignantly pervert idea, ingrained in samsaric beings, known as the perception of permanence in the impermanent, anicce niccasanna, which prevents them from seeing the inherent transience of eye and forms. That is how the six spheres of sense create a world before us.
tts_line: There is a malignantly pervert idea, ingrained in samsaric beings, known as the perception of permanence in the impermanent, anicce niccasanna, which prevents them from seeing the inherent transience of eye and forms. That is how the six spheres of sense create a world before us.

nanananda_verbatim:
From whatever source papañcasaññāsankhā beset a man, if, in regard to
that, there is nothing to be delighted in, asserted, or clung to, then
this itself is the end of the underlying tendencies to attachment, to
aversion, to views, to doubts, to conceit, to attachment towards
existence, and to ignorance.
plain_english_below: From whatever source papancasannasankha beset a man, if, in regard to that, there is nothing to be delighted in, asserted, or clung to, then this itself is the end of the underlying tendencies to attachment, to aversion, to views, to doubts, to conceit, to attachment towards existence, and to not seeing how it works.
tts_line: From whatever source papancasannasankha beset a man, if, in regard to that, there is nothing to be delighted in, asserted, or clung to, then this itself is the end of the underlying tendencies to attachment, to aversion, to views, to doubts, to conceit, to attachment towards existence, and to not seeing how it works.

nanananda_verbatim:
The tendency to grasp a sign in regard to the objects of the six
senses is the result of the perception of permanence. Due to the
perception of permanence, there is a grasping of signs, and due to that
grasping of signs, influxes flow in. Proliferations through craving,
conceits and views get heaped up. This is how our world is
constructed.
plain_english_below: The tendency to grasp a sign in regard to the objects of the six senses is the result of the perception of permanence. Due to the perception of permanence, there is a holding on of signs, and due to that holding on of signs, influxes flow in. Proliferations through craving, conceits and views get heaped up. This is how our world is constructed.
tts_line: The tendency to grasp a sign in regard to the objects of the six senses is the result of the perception of permanence. Due to the perception of permanence, there is a holding on of signs, and due to that holding on of signs, influxes flow in. Proliferations through craving, conceits and views get heaped up. This is how our world is constructed.

nanananda_verbatim:
Earth, water, fire, air, beings, gods, Pajapati, Brahma... the seen,
the heard, the sensed, the cognised, unity, diversity, all, Nibbana.
plain_english_below: Earth, water, fire, air, beings, gods, Pajapati, Brahma... the seen, the heard, the sensed, the cognised, unity, diversity, all, Nibbana (out, like a flame with no fuel).
tts_line: Earth, water, fire, air, beings, gods, Pajapati, Brahma... the seen, the heard, the sensed, the cognised, unity, diversity, all, Nibbana — out, like a flame with no fuel.

nanananda_verbatim:
It is because of our saṃsāric habit of taking in signs that thoughts
and proliferations arise in us.
plain_english_below: It is because of our samsaric habit of taking in signs that thoughts and proliferations arise in us.
tts_line: It is because of our samsaric habit of taking in signs that thoughts and proliferations arise in us.

nanananda_verbatim:
One might think that a house is made up of tiles and bricks, but tiles
and bricks themselves come to be because of a house. There is a mutual
relationship between them.
plain_english_below: One might think that a house is made up of tiles and bricks, but tiles and bricks themselves come to be because of a house. There is a mutual relationship between them.
tts_line: One might think that a house is made up of tiles and bricks, but tiles and bricks themselves come to be because of a house. There is a mutual relationship between them.

nanananda_verbatim:
These fetters are called saṃyojanāni. A binding or a fetter implies
'two', as when two bulls are tied together. The term upādāna... implies
a holding on to something. There, too, the notion of a duality comes
in — one who holds and the thing held.
plain_english_below: These fetters are called samyojanani. A binding or a fetter implies 'two', as when two bulls are tied together. The term upadana... implies a holding on to something. There, too, the notion of a duality comes in — one who holds and the thing held.
tts_line: These fetters are called samyojanani. A binding or a fetter implies 'two', as when two bulls are tied together. The term upadana... implies a holding on to something. There, too, the notion of a duality comes in — one who holds and the thing held.

nanananda_verbatim:
Na nimittaggāhi nānuvyañjanaggāhī — 'he doesn't grasp a sign nor does
he dwell on its details'.

nanananda_verbatim:
The discrimination between an 'internal' and an 'external' is the
outcome of the inability to penetrate name-and-form, to see through it.
There is an apparent duality: I, as one who sees, and name-and-form, as
the objects seen. Between them there is a dichotomy as internal and
external. It is on this very dichotomy that the six sense-bases are
'based'.
plain_english_below: The discrimination between an 'internal' and an 'external' is the outcome of the inability to penetrate name-and-form, to see through it. There is an apparent duality: I, as one who sees, and name-and-form, as the objects seen. Between them there is a dichotomy as internal and external. It is on this very dichotomy that the six sense-bases are 'based'.

nanananda_verbatim:
There is a certain deep significance in the word yathabhuta. In
contradistinction to the two words bhava and vibhava, the word bhuta
has some peculiarity of its own.
plain_english_below: There is a certain deep significance in the word yathabhuta. In contradistinction to the two words bhava (the next me forming) and vibhava, the word bhuta has some peculiarity of its own.
